Client shall promptly notify TrueLink of any such claim, TrueLink shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim, and Client shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.

quote: b. TrueLink shall indemnify and hold Client harmless, its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents and licensors harmless from and against all claims, actions, expenses, losses, and liabilities, including reasonable attorneys' fees, arising from or relating to any
rationale: Section 12(b) gives only a breach-of-contract indemnity from TrueLink (no duty to defend, no IP infringement, breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct cover, and no defence procedure), while Section 12(a) imposes a very broad Client indemnity covering Client's breach of the Agreement, System/Credit Repository Agreement defaults, Web Site claims generally and product/service injury. That fails the fallback (no Vendor IP indemnity anywhere in the document) and approaches walk-away territory. We added a TrueLink defence and indemnity for third-party IP, breach of applicable law, TrueLink-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct with notice, control and cooperation, and limited our indemnity to Client Content and Client's violations of law by removing the breach-of-Agreement, System Agreement default, Web Site and product-injury prongs. We did not add the fallback 3× super-cap or procure/modify/replace/refund mechanic, which belong to the fallback level and would newly limit TrueLink's exposure.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete: the cap is expressly mutual ("EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY"), the existing 12-month hosting-and-support fee basis is retained verbatim, and indemnification, confidentiality breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are all placed outside the limitation for both parties. Preferred level is not reached: no USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid" rather than "paid or payable", 12 months not anchored to the event giving rise to the claim, no mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or IP infringement, nor an exclusion of Client payment obligations from capped damages. Minimality holds: only two edits were made — the party reference was mutualised and the existing GN/WM parenthetical was expanded into the four-item carve-out list. The removed words ("DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S") sit inside the gross negligence / wilful misconduct carve-out element itself, and the Section 3, 4, 7 and 11 scope, the cap amount language and all surrounding text are untouched. No survival tails, procedures or extra damages categories were added. Intent is preserved: no defined term is left undefined (TrueLink is now covered by "either party"), no cross-reference dangles, and the retained indemnity in Section 12a is not contradicted because indemnification obligations are expressly outside the cap. Residual note for the drafter (not a defect at fallback): if the Agreement charges compensation other than for hosting and support services, the retained cap basis captures only a subset of fees; if a subsequent round is available, replace it with "fees paid or payable by Client under this Agreement" and add the USD 1,000,000 floor, the event-anchored 12-month window, a mutual consequential-damages waiver, and the data protection/security, fraud and IP carve-outs plus the payment-obligations exclusion to reach the preferred position.

quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.

verification.notes: All six preferred elements are met in operative language: the Client affiliate/successor no-approval carve-out, the mutual approval requirement retained against TrueLink, the reasonableness qualifier, the competitor bar, and the express statement that a Client change of control gives TrueLink no termination right. The fallback level is not complete (one-sided successor right, no written-notice mechanic, retained Client affiliate exception), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is complete. Minimality holds: the edit inserts one qualifying phrase, narrows the pre-existing exception to Client (necessary, since a retained mutual affiliate exception would defeat "Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent"), and adds one short sentence carrying only the two remaining checklist elements. No survival tails, procedures, or unrelated boilerplate were added. Minor observation only (not a defect): the reasonableness standard is drafted mutually, so it also constrains Client's withholding of consent; this is the most concise placement and is consistent with the playbook's fallback formulation. Intent is preserved: the mutual approval architecture, section numbering, and all unrelated commercial mechanics survive; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and the change-of-control sentence contradicts nothing because the document contains no change-of-control trigger. Deviation status is correct: the original clause failed the fallback on material terms (no successor/M&A carve-out for Client, no notice mechanic, unqualified approval standard) and its mutual "financially responsible affiliate" exception let TrueLink assign to affiliates without Client's approval.

The only sourcing-style covenant, Section 3(i) ("Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface"), is conditioned on Client's voluntary use of the Interface and does not restrict Client from using alternatives, so it is not exclusivity. quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages or penalty on Client, so it sits at the preferred position. Compensation (§5) obliges Client only to pay fees for services actually requested, subject to stated monthly minimums that are ongoing service charges for periods in which the services are supplied — not a stipulated sum triggered by termination or breach. Termination (§14) lets Client elect to terminate on written notice with service (and therefore fees) simply running to the last day of the following month; no exit fee, accelerated remaining-term charge, or minimum-fee buyout applies. The term/non-renewal provision (§13), the spam covenants (§§7 and 8f, which reserve only TrueLink's ordinary legal and equitable remedies), the indemnity (§12) and the attorney-fee clause (§28) likewise create no fixed or pre-agreed damages amount payable by Client. Because absence of any Customer-payable liquidated amount achieves the preferred outcome, no redline is proposed; we would resist any later insertion of an exit fee above three months' fees.

quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
rationale: Section 14 gives Client an unconditional election to terminate the Agreement on written notice, with service continuing only until the last day of the month following notice (roughly 30–60 days). That is a Customer convenience right no more onerous than the 60–90 days' notice contemplated at the fallback, and no early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere (Section 5 bills monthly in arrears against invoices paid within 15 days of receipt), so the fee cap element is satisfied a fortiori. On the Vendor side there is no mid-term convenience right at all: Section 13 lets Sections 2 and 3 fall away only for Client breach/default (a for-cause trigger), and TrueLink's only other exit is a notice of intent not to renew at the end of the one-year term, which is a natural-term non-renewal question under RENEWAL (30 days' notice) rather than a T4C convenience termination, so we do not flag it twice here. The bargain therefore sits at or above the fallback and we would not redline it. Two points short of the preferred wording are noted for information only, not as deviations: the notice mechanic can run past 30 days where notice is given early in a month, and there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (of limited practical effect given monthly arrears invoicing).

quote: Client will pay TrueLink's fees for requested Hosting Services and Support Services pursuant to the schedule of charges set forth on Exhibits "A" and "B" attached hereto, (but not less than $____ per month for the Hosting Services and $____ per month for Support Services).
rationale: Section 5(a) does impose a minimum monthly spend on Client for Hosting and Support Services (a take-or-pay floor), so the preferred position (no minimum commitment, pay only for usage/ordered Services) is not met. It does, however, sit at the fallback on its material terms: (i) the commitment is bounded by a 12-month term — Section 13 fixes the term at one year, and each automatic renewal is a fresh one-year term that Client can stop on thirty (30) days' notice of intent not to renew, so there is no multi-year lock-in; (ii) Client has an unconditional exit on roughly a month's notice — Section 14 lets Client elect to terminate at any time, with services (and therefore the minimums) running only to the last day of the month following the notice month; and (iii) there is no shortfall penalty, liquidated damages or accelerated-minimum mechanic anywhere — the floor is simply a monthly fee that ceases on termination, so nothing punitive needs converting to a true-up. This is comfortably outside walk-away territory (multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right). Minor points noted but not redlined: the exit is a full termination rather than a partial reduction and can run to ~59 days rather than exactly 30; there is no express true-up credit; Section 14's "Subject to Section 4" and Section 6's reference to "minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4" (the minimums are in Section 5) are loose cross-references worth tidying, and Section 6 bars Client from contesting or obtaining backup for the minimum fees. verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete: both elements are rendered as operative, unconditional obligations of TrueLink at exactly the fallback limits (E&O USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy USD 2,000,000), with no undefined trigger and no internal inconsistency. Preferred level is incomplete: CGL per-occurrence and aggregate limits, E&O at USD 2,000,000, cyber at USD 5,000,000, workers' compensation, and certificates on request are all absent. This is disclosed in the rationale rather than promised in operative language, which is the correct treatment for a fallback-level proposal. Minimality holds: the insertion adds only the two required coverages and omits model-language extras that no selected element requires (at-its-own-expense, term-plus-one-year survival tail, CGL, workers' compensation, certificates). No existing text was deleted or paraphrased — Section 30 (Force Majeure) is retained verbatim. Intent preserved: the clause is placed after Section 30 and before signatures, leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict the indemnity at Section 12 or the miscellaneous provisions; insurance and indemnity remain independent allocations. Drafting nit only (not a defect requiring repair for completeness): the inserted heading "INSURANCE." carries no section number, so it should be numbered (e.g., "31. INSURANCE.") to match the Agreement's numbering convention. If TrueLink pushes back, note that the position sits at the fallback and the preferred schedule (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, workers' comp, certificates on request) remains available.
